For examples, see the i18n folder.

styles_modal.heading: Styles ℹ
styles_modal.heading_desc:
Styles allow hotswapping of textures to create multiple outfits/skins.

The first active style containing the bone's texture name will be used.
styles_modal.style_preview_empty:
No textures in this style.

Click to select and add to it.
styles_modal.texture_desc:
Drag to a bone to set this as it's texture.
Drag above/below another texture to change order.
styles_modal.assigned_textures_desc:
Assign textures to bones here.

If this style is inactive, bones will switch to a texture of the same name from the first active style top-down.
styles_modal.same_name: There is already a texture with the same name in this style.
styles_modal.styles_empty:
All textures must be in a style.

Styles are batches of textures, used to represent outfits or skins.

To add a style, click 'New' above.
styles_modal.textures_empty:
This style's textures will appear here.

Click 'New > Import' above to import an image to add as a texture.
styles_modal.assigned_empty:
Once a texture is added, the bone hierarchy will be shown on the left.

All bones' assigned textures will be shown here.

atlas_modal.heading: Importing Texture(s)
atlas_modal.no_pending:
If the imported image is a single texture, simply click 'Done'.

If it's a texture atlas, drag the image or click 'Add Texture' to add a new slice of texture.

The atlas will be discarded once done, and will need to be re-imported to add more textures.

export_modal.heading: Export
export_modal.no_anims:
Export unavailable - no animations.

To export the rest pose, create an empty animation.

armature.bake_ik_desc:
If ticked, inverse kinematics will be baked into all animations where targets are moved.

Recommended if inverse kinematics is only used in animations, especially if developing your own runtime.
armature.exclude_ik_desc:
Inverse kinematics will be assumed off when exporting.

Recommended to prevent runtimes from mixing up baked and real-time inverse kinematics.
armature.clear_color_desc: The color that transparent pixels will be represented by

dragonbones.desc:
Writes <name>_ske.json, <name>_tex.json and <name>_tex.png (DragonBones 5.5 JSON) next to the chosen file.

Only the active style is exported, as a single atlas. Inverse kinematics is baked into rotations; physics is not exported.

image.image_sequences_desc: Instead of using sheets, sprites will be exported individually
image.animations_check_desc: Include this animation in the export?

video.use_system_ffmpeg_desc: Use the ffmpeg installed on your system (in your PATH) instead of the one downloaded below.
video.system_ffmpeg_note:
Video export uses the ffmpeg installed on your system.
Install it with your package manager (Linux) or 'brew install ffmpeg' (macOS).
video.global_bounds_desc: If enabled, all videos will have consistent dimensions

armature_panel.heading: Armature
armature_panel.styles_desc:
Create a style, add textures, then assign bones to use it. Click on styles in the dropdown to toggle them.

Bones use textures based on their index. To change it, select a bone > 'Tex Index'.

Multiple styles can be active at once. Bones assinged to multiple active styles will use the top-most first.

icons.ik_tip: Inverse kinematics, turning $chain bone(s) above this one

bind_pose.label: Bind Pose ℹ:
bind_pose.desc:
Bind pose skinning: vertices blended across several bones follow each bone relative to where it was when bound, like in 3D software. Weights can be edited freely without vertices moving.

The bind pose always follows the setup pose.

Works by adding greyed-out helper bones (name__bind__mesh), so any SkelForm runtime plays it unchanged.
bind_pose.set_desc: Use bind pose skinning for this mesh. Best turned on before adding vertices to binds.
bind_pose.all_desc: Use bind pose skinning for every mesh in the armature that has binds
bind_pose.path_desc: Meshes with path binds can't use bind pose skinning
bind_pose.clear_desc: Go back to classic binds. Vertices blended across several bones may shift.
bind_pose.helper_note: This is a Bind Pose helper bone. It is managed automatically and can't be edited.

bone_panel.heading: Bone
bone_panel.name: Name:
bone_panel.global_zindex_inc_desc:
Raise this z-index, as well as all z-indexes higher than this, by 1.

Useful for fixing 'same z-index' warnings.
bone_panel.bone_empty:
This bone currently has no texture and is an invisible point.

To add a texture to it, assign one via the Textures setup above.

This bone may be dragged in the Armature list, to change its order or to assign it as a child to another bone.
bone_panel.length_to_child_desc:
Set the length to the distance to this bone's first child.

The length runs along the bone's own axis. To point the bone at its child too, Ctrl+drag its tail handle (this turns the bone and its art).
bone_panel.group_color_desc:
Color used to represent this bone and it's children.

Set alpha to 0 to use default color.

skin.label: Skin ℹ:
skin.desc: Skin this mesh to the skeleton, with weights from the bones' envelopes.
skin.bind_desc:
Bind every selected mesh to the skeleton in one step: turns on Bind Pose, binds each skeleton bone within reach, and weights every vertex from the bones' envelopes.

Skeleton bones are the ones set to Deform (by default, bones without a texture). Run it again after adding bones or changing lengths; vertices you weighted by hand keep their weights.
skin.envelope_weights_desc:
Weights follow the bones' envelopes, and update when envelopes, lengths or the setup pose change.

Untick to keep the current weights as plain hand weights.
skin.max_influences_desc: The most bones that can move one vertex. Game runtimes usually support 4.
skin.add_in_reach_desc: Bind every skeleton bone whose envelope reaches this mesh.
skin.locked_desc: Vertices whose weights were edited by hand. Envelope updates leave them alone.
skin.outside_desc: These vertices sit outside every bone's envelope, so they follow their nearest bone fully. Widen an envelope, or weight them by hand.
skin.pose_mode: Binding uses the rest pose: switch from Pose to the Armature or Animation tab.
skin.outside_report: Bound to the skeleton. $err vertices sit outside every envelope and follow their nearest bone fully; the mesh panel can select them.

envelope.heading: Envelope
envelope.desc: The area around this bone that skins meshes bound to the skeleton: full influence inside the inner radius, fading out to the outer radius.
envelope.deform_desc: This bone is part of the skeleton and skins meshes. On by default for bones without a texture.
envelope.head: Head ℹ:
envelope.radius_desc: Inner and outer radius (px) at this end of the bone. Bones without length use the head's.
envelope.falloff_desc: How influence fades between the inner and outer radius.
envelope.absolute_desc: Full influence anywhere inside the outer radius. For rigid pieces like a hand or a sword.

inverse_kinematics.heading: Inverse Kinematics
inverse_kinematics.desc:
Turn the bones above this one so its origin reaches a target bone. Move the target to pose the chain.

Solving keeps the pose as drawn: adding IK, or a target sitting where this bone already is, moves nothing.
inverse_kinematics.enabled_desc:
Run this IK constraint.

Untick it to edit the rest layout of its chain (positions and rotations the solver otherwise controls).
inverse_kinematics.add_desc: Make this bone the tip of an IK chain, with a new target bone where it's drawn now.
inverse_kinematics.target_space_desc:
What the target follows. World keeps it where it is when the body moves, which grounds feet. A bone, such as the chest for an arm, makes it move with that bone, so the hand follows the upper body.

Switching keeps the target where it is. Keyframes already on the target stay as they are, relative to its new parent.
inverse_kinematics.target_in_chain: That bone can't be the target: it's in this IK chain, or under it, so moving the chain would move the target too.
inverse_kinematics.chain_desc: How many bones above this one the IK turns. 2 suits an arm or a leg.
inverse_kinematics.bend_desc:
Which way the chain bends at its joints.

As drawn: the way it bends now.
CW: turns clockwise at each joint.
CCW: turns counter-clockwise at each joint.
inverse_kinematics.weight_desc: How much the IK applies: 1 reaches the target, 0 shows the animated pose. Animate it to switch between IK and keyframed rotation.
inverse_kinematics.copy_rotation_desc: This bone takes the target's rotation, like a hand or a foot following its target.
inverse_kinematics.cant_edit:
Inverse kinematics controls this.

To edit it, untick the IK constraint on the chain's tip bone, or move its target.

mesh_deformation.heading: Mesh Deformation
mesh_deformation.desc: Turn this texture into a deformable mesh. Vertices can be bound to other bones with custom weights to influence them.
mesh_deformation.trace_desc: Generate a mesh based on the texture shape
mesh_deformation.trace_finish_desc: Finish tracing and hide tracing options
mesh_deformation.pathing_desc: Vertices will follow this bind along a path formed with adjacent binds.
mesh_deformation.no_bound_verts:
Double-click on vertices to add or remove them to this bind.

Vertex weights will be configurable here.
mesh_deformation.padding_desc: How far (pixels) the outline sits outside the art, so soft edges stay inside the mesh
mesh_deformation.trace_detail_desc: How closely (pixels) the outline follows the art. Lower is more faithful; higher uses fewer vertices
mesh_deformation.trace_density_desc:
Target size (pixels) of the triangles inside the mesh. Smaller gives more vertices to bend with.

0 gives an outline-only mesh
mesh_deformation.trace_alpha_desc: Pixels at least this opaque (1-255) count as art
mesh_deformation.trace_outline_desc:
Trace just the outline, with no vertices inside, to cut the shape out and draw its topology yourself (e.g. with the Pen tool).

The inside is still split into triangles between outline vertices, since a mesh is made of triangles.

physics.heading: Physics
physics.sway_desc:
When this bone's parent moves, it will sway against the momentum.
Useful for tails, clothes, hair, etc
physics.parent_has_physics: This bone's parent has rotation physics. Adjust its distance in the Physics section below. ℹ
physics.parent_has_physics_desc: To accurately simulate wind/air resistance, bones should only be distanced horizontally to their parent.

editing.heading: Editing
editing.edit_while_playing_desc:
By default, edits won't be recorded if an animation is playing to prevent accidents.

Tick this allow editing while an animation is playing.
editing.propagate_visibility_desc:
By default, bones do not propagate their current visibily onto their children.

This is to replicate simple runtime behavior, where propagation is likely to not be implemented.
editing.bone_translucency_desc: How transparent (0-1) other bones should be if not selected

rendering.heading: Rendering
rendering.translucent_desc: Makes this box translucent to preview rendering changes
rendering.attachment_display: Show textured bones as attachments ℹ:
rendering.attachment_display_desc:
Draw bones that show a texture as a small dot with a thin line to their parent, instead of a full bone.

Keeps the rig (bones) visually separate from the art (textures).
rendering.mesh_edge_outline_desc: A faint dark outline along mesh edges, so they stay visible on light and dark art.
rendering.bind_weight_colors: Color bind vertices by weight ℹ:
rendering.bind_weight_colors_desc:
While a bind is selected, each of its vertices gets its own color, matching its row in the bind panel.

A pale tint means weight 0; full color means weight 1.

keyboard.heading: Keyboard
keyboard.timeline_zoom_mode_desc: The timeline editor will zoom, instead of scroll, when scrolling and holding this modifier.
keyboard.tool_pen_desc: Draw edges on the selected mesh: click to place points, Enter to apply.
keyboard.tool_eraser_desc: Erase vertices and edges of the selected mesh by clicking or dragging over them.
keyboard.tool_pan_desc: Drag with the left mouse button to move the view. Right-drag pans in every tool.
keyboard.fit_view_desc: Frame the selected bone, or the whole armature if none is selected.

miscellaneous.heading: Miscellaneous
miscellaneous.select_exact_bone: Select exact bone in click ℹ:
miscellaneous.select_exact_bone_desc: Clicking on a bone that is named 'Texture' (any case) will select the parent. Tick this to directly select the texture.
miscellaneous.keep_tex_str: Keep texture name after renaming ℹ:
miscellaneous.keep_tex_str_desc: By default, renaming a texture will also adjust bones using it to change their tex name. Tick this to preserve bone texture names after renaming.
miscellaneous.use_fallback_desc:
If the current language is missing any localization, the English version will be used by default.

Tick this to force all missing texts to show their key instead.

keyframe_editor.heading: Animation
keyframe_editor.invalid_fps:
Some keyframes will be lost.

Potential fixes:
- Spread out keyframes
- Incrementally change FPS
keyframe_editor.set_key_desc: Key the selected bones' position, rotation and scale on this frame, as they are shown now, to hold a pose. Moving, rotating or scaling a bone while animating keys it automatically.
keyframe_editor.key_all_desc: Key every bone without a texture (the skeleton, and controls like IK targets) on this frame, as shown now.
keyframe_editor.breakdown_desc: Key the selected bones on this frame between their previous and next keys: 0% is the previous pose, 100% the next, 50% halfway. Drag to set it live.
keyframe_editor.delete_key_desc: Remove the selected bones' keys on this frame, or every key on it when no bone is selected.
keyframe_editor.zoom_kb_tip: Tip - hold $kb to zoom in/out by scrolling
keyframe_editor.double_click_tip: Double-click to select related keyframes in this bone

keyframe_panel.empty:
Nothing to edit, as this is the first frame.

To adjust this keyframe's transition, select the one after it.
keyframe_panel.snap_note:
With this preset, values will snap between keyframes instead of interpolating.

To re-enable the graph, change the preset above.

warnings.heading: Warnings ℹ
warnings.desc:
These are quirks that need your attention to fix.
Runtimes may have issues with this armature if not dealt with.
warnings.OnlyPath: $bone can't have a single bind that's a path.
warnings.IkTargetInChain: $bone's IK target is in its own chain, or under it.
warnings.NoWeights: $bone's bind $bind has all weights set to 0.
warnings.ClassicMultiBind: $bone has $count vertices in more than one bind. Classic binds place these out of position; turn on Bind Pose for this mesh (in the mesh panel) before binding to blend them correctly.

toolbar.zoom_desc:
Zoom

Click to zoom in, Alt+click to zoom out, or drag left and right.
toolbar.fit_desc: Fit View: frame the selected bone, or the whole armature
toolbar.pen_desc:
Click to place points, each joined to the last. Cuts split the triangles they cross; closed loops and cuts out from the mesh and back fill new area.

Enter: apply   Esc: cancel   Right-click: end cut   Backspace: remove point
Shift: no snapping   Ctrl: edge midpoint   C: 45° lock
toolbar.pen_hint: Enter: apply · Esc: cancel · RMB: end cut
toolbar.pen_snap_desc: Snap to vertices and edges (hold Shift to place freely)
toolbar.pen_angle_desc: Keep new segments at multiples of 45° (C)
toolbar.eraser_desc: Click or drag over vertices and edges to erase them. Each stroke is one undo step.
toolbar.eraser_dissolve_desc: Remove the vertex or edge but keep the surface: the gap is filled from its neighbours
toolbar.eraser_delete_desc: Remove the vertex or edge and the triangles that use it, leaving a hole
toolbar.envelope_desc:
See and size bone envelopes, which weight meshes bound to the skeleton.

Drag a diamond to resize the inner or outer radius at that end of the selected bone; Shift sizes both ends. With a bone selected, the meshes it skins show its weight on each vertex, from blue (none) to red (full); white rings mark vertices weighted by hand.
toolbar.envelope_label_desc: This bone's bind index in the selected mesh. Click to select the bind, then click vertices (while editing the mesh) to add them to it.
toolbar.envelope_show_all_desc: Show every deforming bone's envelope, to check how they overlap at joints.
toolbar.needs_texture: Select a bone with a texture to use this tool.
toolbar.retriangulate_desc: Replace the triangles with an automatic (Delaunay) triangulation of the current vertices

pose.heading: Pose
pose.desc:
Pose Mode: move bones freely to test how meshes deform, without changing the rest (setup) pose.

Turning it off puts every bone back. Pose Mode edits aren't kept in undo history, and saving always saves the rest pose.
